title: The flat roof is a jumble of stepped sand blocks with no continuous parapet, and
why: The jumbled stepped sand roof is replaced by a continuous light parapet ringing a flat roof with a tidy dark beam fascia and protruding vigas, which reads as the intended flat-roofed adobe form, though the single small block on the roof is a bit plain.

title: The back and side walls are flat, smooth slabs. The wall is not thick or rounded
why: The side wall in the second view gains some stepped relief, which addresses the flat-slab complaint, but it is offset by small stair-like blocks at the base that read as loose bits, and the first view changes only a minor pilaster and a step, so the net effect is roughly as good as before.

title: The roof levels and upper blocks are placed irregularly. The front arcade is sha
why: The change adds stepped sandstone masses and blocks in front of the arcade that cover the awnings and entrance, reading as clutter and broken, unsupported bits rather than a cleaner roof or upper-wall fix.

title: The vigas are chunky dark cubes that read as floating blocks at the roofline. Th
why: The before and after views look nearly identical: the roofline vigas are still chunky dark cubes, and the only visible addition is a small dark dot on top of the wind tower, so the change is too subtle to call an improvement or a regression.

title: Pots and baskets are small and clustered at the front only, and there is no sign
why: The after view adds a clear sign on the upper wall and spreads potted plants and small lit details along the arcade instead of clustering them at the front, which reads as a lived-in market, though the small stepped plinths under the side plants look a little fiddly.

title: Readable BAZAAR name board over the portal
why: The task asked for a readable BAZAAR board, but the after-image letters read as "8-ZAAN" with the B and R malformed and the last letter clipped at the edge, while the grey plates clash with the warm sandstone and terracotta palette and sit as a loud band above the awnings.

title: Real arch head on the portal
why: The portal head still reads as a rectangular wood block rather than an arch, and the change adds a dark offset notch on the right and a dark recessed slab under the lintel that look like stray, unexplained blocks in the oblique view.

title: Orange ring on the dome
why: The orange terracotta ring turns the bare flat top into a defined parapet around the dome base, matching the brief's parapet and palette, with no floating or broken bits, though its stepped corners are a little blocky.

title: Wind tower slits and cap
why: The after view adds dark wood-framed slits on the wind tower's faces and a sandstone cap block on top, so the tower reads more clearly as a finished tower, though the small dark stripe on the cap edge is a minor stray detail.

title: Awning valance and pennants
why: The after view adds orange pennant banners on the outer wall edges that read as deliberate market dressing, and the lower storefront bays look tidier with uniform dark slatted panels in place of the mixed openings, with no floating or clashing bits visible.
